title: OAB Evolution Trigger
description: A standing hypothesis with a falsification test: the measurable condition under which an architectural decision must be revisited. Triggers are what turn a design from a document that rots into a system that tells you when it has expired.

id.description: Stable, kebab-case, unique within the project.

metric.description: What is measured. Must be observable today, or the trigger includes the work to instrument it — otherwise it never fires.

source.description: WHERE the metric is read: a named dashboard, tool, or review. If you cannot name where it is read, it is not a trigger — it is a hope.

threshold.description: Set with headroom before the cliff. A trigger at 95% CPU fires during the incident, not before it.

window.description: The sustained period over which the condition must hold. Instantaneous triggers fire on spikes and get ignored, which is worse than having no trigger.

action.description: The next step, not the answer. 'Re-run capacity analysis and evaluate options' is right; 'add a message broker' pre-decides the outcome the analysis is supposed to reach.

owner.description: A person, role, or team. Unowned triggers are decoration.

verification.description: How often someone confirms the metric is still emitted and the threshold still meaningful. Triggers rot when the dashboard they name is retired.

status.description: armed = watching; fired = the condition was met; resolved = fired and acted on; retired = no longer relevant.

fired_at.description: Retained after resolution rather than cleared, so the history of when an architecture actually strained is preserved.

then.description: A trigger that fired must record when.
